# Halcyon Threshold — Strategy (draft, 16 Nov 2026)

## Mission
Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.
Kept deliberately open-ended per Morgan's instruction — this doc is the current
best guess, not a fixed charter.

## Constraints (real, not hypothetical)
- Time: evenings and weekends only. Morgan still works full-time at Dorrance Logistics.
- Money: up to ~$2,000 of personal savings this year. Not more, without outside funding.
- **Employment clause (critical path item):** Morgan's Dorrance contract (sec. 7)
  requires disclosure/approval before outside roles, paid outside work, or public
  statements made in a professional capacity. Morgan has said he doesn't want his
  name on anything public — posts, letters, press — until that conversation happens.
  It hasn't happened yet. Dorrance's annual outside-activities disclosure is also due
  30 Nov. **Until this is resolved, nothing public goes out under Morgan's name or
  Halcyon Threshold's — no press quotes, no open-letter signatures, no published
  site, no public comments, no grant applications where Morgan is the named
  accountable party.** This is the single biggest bottleneck on the whole project
  right now and is squarely Morgan's to resolve, not the agent's.
- Skills on hand: writing, workable Python, no deep ML research background.
- One volunteer has already surfaced: Priya Raman, data analyst, ~5 hrs/week.

## Why this shape of project
Morgan's own framing (from notes): "evals for something nobody is measuring" is the
idea with the best fit to actual skills (writing + scripting, not frontier research),
the best chance of being genuinely useful (most independent attention clusters on
the two or three biggest labs; almost nothing tracks the next tier down), and the
easiest to make concrete and fundable.

## Proposed first workstream: Safety-Practices Scorecard for non-frontier developers
A public, versioned rubric scoring well-resourced AI developers *outside* the top
2-3 frontier labs on: eval-methodology transparency, red-team cadence and
disclosure, dangerous-capability eval coverage, incident-reporting practice, and
pre-deployment review process. Initial cohort ~15-20 developers, scored from public
filings/docs/API documentation, published with full methodology, refreshed
quarterly. See `draft-emberfall-proposal.md` for a fundable version of this.

This is neglected, measurable, writable by one person plus a part-time analyst,
and produces something citable (a thing other people — journalists, policymakers,
Alignment Commons readers — can point to), which is the kind of leverage a single
outsider can actually have.

## Other ideas considered, parked for now
- Reading group — low leverage, many already exist, revisit only if it becomes a
  pipeline into volunteers/collaborators.
- Small-grants regranting — needs capital and credibility Halcyon Threshold doesn't
  have yet. Revisit after the scorecard project establishes a track record.
- Newsletter — "probably too many already," per Morgan's own notes. Agreed; skip.

## Sequencing
1. Resolve the Dorrance HR disclosure (Morgan, personally, this week — it's gating
   the grant application, the open letter, the press quote, and site publication).
2. Finalize and submit the Emberfall rapid-grant proposal if HR clears in time
   (deadline 30 Nov) — draft ready in `draft-emberfall-proposal.md`.
3. Once there's a funded or self-funded go-ahead: build the rubric, recruit Priya
   (or similar) for the data work, score the first cohort.
4. Publish the scorecard; only then does a public Halcyon Threshold presence
   (website, social, bylines) make sense — it'll have something to point to.

## Live external opportunities being tracked (not yet acted on)
See `pending-decisions.md`.

## Halcyon Threshold — Safety-Practices Scorecard for Non-Frontier AI Developers

### What we'll do
Build and publish an independent, versioned scorecard rating well-resourced AI
developers *outside* the two or three most-scrutinized frontier labs on five public
indicators: eval-methodology transparency, red-team cadence/disclosure,
dangerous-capability eval coverage, incident-reporting practice, and pre-deployment
review process. Score an initial cohort of 15-20 developers from public filings,
documentation, and model cards. Publish the full methodology alongside the scores.
